title: Durably record the safe-boundary observation for a released attempt
description:
Objective: produce the safe-boundary facts `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` requires and nothing in production currently writes. Third producer repair for task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4, per its rail 1: "if it omits a named fact, repair that producer rather than reconstructing authority here."

MEASURED GAP at HEAD fa39721 across apps/daemon/src (non-test). Two fields of `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` (packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-planning-hold.ts:31,33) have ZERO production producers:
- `safeBoundaryObserved` — ZERO hits anywhere in apps/daemon.
- `observationRef` — ZERO hits.

THE WIRE KIND ALREADY EXISTS. `safe_boundary.observe` is a member of the frozen `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85), so this capability was designed in and reserved a command kind — it simply has no daemon producer and no registry entry. That is a meaningful difference from the coordination surface, whose kind was never in the union at all: here the union already permits it, so this task does NOT need a contracts expansion and is not blocked by the M5 closed-union ruling. Verify that membership yourself before planning, and note that `runtime-envelope.ts:142` refuses any kind outside the union before `http-adapter.ts:196` reads the registry — so a kind already present is exactly what makes this reachable.

Deliverable: a durable safe-boundary observation for an attempt, recorded by production, carrying `safeBoundaryObserved` and the `observationRef` that identifies the observation. An observation is a FACT ABOUT WHAT WAS SEEN, not a declaration that things are safe: an agent must not be able to assert its own boundary was observed, which is the whole reason this field exists separately from the terminality flags.

Consider whether the observation is best produced by registering `safe_boundary.observe` in the daemon command registry (it is already in the union, already gated by capability), by the release path observing the boundary itself, or both. State the choice and its reason; if a registry entry is the answer, follow the shape `RECOVERY_COMPLETION_COMMAND_KIND` already uses as a singleton kind with its own capability, payload allow-list and family entry.

NOT in scope: release disposition, lease or slot state (task-740924b7); terminal effect and resource refs (task-6d400781); the evidence reader itself (task-e62e3828); creating a hold, PlanningRun, or scheduler admission.

Owned paths: one new module under apps/daemon/src/ plus its .js bridge and focused test, and — only if the registry route is chosen — apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "safeBoundaryObserved\|observationRef" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v fixtures` returns production producers where both returned zero.

The observation records WHAT WAS SEEN, not what a caller asserted: a test supplies a caller-claimed `safeBoundaryObserved: true` for a boundary that was not observed and asserts the claim is refused with an exact code and layer, never recorded.
An unobserved or unreadable boundary yields `safeBoundaryObserved: false` or a typed UNKNOWN and blocks release — never an assumed true. A test drives each and pins the exact code and layer.

`observationRef` identifies a durable observation that can be read back; a test resolves the ref and asserts it returns the same observation, and a ref pointing at nothing is refused rather than accepted as an identifier.

If the registry route is chosen: the command uses the ALREADY-PRESENT `safe_boundary.observe` kind from the frozen union — no contracts expansion — with its own capability and payload allow-list, and a test asserts an unauthenticated or malformed send is refused with its exact code and layer.
A mutation that defaults `safeBoundaryObserved` to true when the observation is missing turns a NAMED test red.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately, the test leg prints a nonzero count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: An observation is a fact about what was SEEN. No caller-supplied `safeBoundaryObserved`, observation ref or boundary claim may become authority — this field exists precisely so an agent cannot declare its own boundary safe.

Use the `safe_boundary.observe` kind already present in the frozen `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS`; do NOT add a new kind. The union is closed for M5 by human decision, and an unknown kind is refused at `runtime-envelope.ts:142` before the registry is read.
Fail closed: unobserved or unreadable is false or UNKNOWN and blocks release, never an assumed true. A default-true is the single defect this record exists to prevent.
Real SqliteEventStore in tests, closed in a `finally` on every exit path. Target <=250 physical lines per production source; commit only owned paths by explicit pathspec.

THE DEFECT THE SECOND TEST FOUND. Writing the END_UNRECORDED case did not simply pass — the writer REFUSED it: `SAFE_BOUNDARY_COMMIT_CONFLICT` with upstream `STORE_INPUT_INVALID: decidedAt must be a canonical UTC timestamp with millisecond precision`. Cause: the `derivedAt` fallback built a DESCRIPTIVE string, `` `wall:${seconds}` ``, and handed it to `commitExpectedVersionDecision` as `decidedAt`. So whenever `launch.completedAt` was null, the commit threw and **NO observation was recorded at all** — the arm that must fail closed to `safeBoundaryObserved: false` produced nothing whatsoever, leaving the release-evidence chain with no record for exactly the case this record exists to cover. That is strictly worse than an untested arm, and it was invisible while no test drove it. This is why QA's rejection was right to call it two tests rather than a stated limit.
FIX: `derivedAt` now resolves to a CANONICAL instant from durable evidence only — `launch.completedAt`, else `launch.startedAt`, else `observedStart.serverWallSeconds` CONVERTED via `new Date(n * 1_000).toISOString()`. That conversion is arithmetic over a durable number, not a clock sample, so the module's "never a clock read" property is intact (no Date.now anywhere). `Number.isFinite` guards the conversion because `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` THROWS rather than returning a value. When none of the three exist there is no durable instant to stamp, and the writer refuses `SAFE_BOUNDARY_RUN_UNREADABLE` / upstream `NO_DURABLE_INSTANT` rather than committing a value the store will reject — fail closed, no vocabulary widened.

ROUTE DECISION, recorded at execution time so QA grades DoD 5 correctly — and re-measured rather than inherited.

**CHOSEN: DERIVE-ON-RELEASE. NO REGISTRY ENTRY in this task. DoD item 5 is therefore CONDITIONAL and DOES NOT APPLY.**

The task description asks for the choice and its reason. The plan proposed derive-on-release; my step-1 measurement at HEAD 79cc053 CONFIRMS it rather than contradicting it, so I proceed without a replan:
- `safe_boundary.observe` is a member of the frozen `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (`runtime-vocabulary.ts:106`) and `grep -rn "safe_boundary" apps/daemon/src` over non-test sources returns **ZERO** — the kind is reserved and unregistered, exactly as the description states.
- **There is no caller to register it FOR.** Rail 1 forbids any caller-supplied boundary claim, so a registered command's only lawful payload is the attempt identity — and the system-runner/wrapper composition that would send it does not exist. The prior handoff (architect-f956ffe1, 2026-08-16) says its capability and payload allow-list "must be measured from the eventual system-runner composition; do not guess now". Registering a kind with a guessed capability and an allow-list nothing calls would be inventing an ingress, not landing a producer.
- The kind stays reserved in the union. Registering it is a separate future task once that composition lands. **No contracts expansion is made here and no new kind is added — task rail 2 satisfied by not touching the union at all.**

**THE COLLISION THE PLAN WARNED ABOUT IS AVOIDABLE ENTIRELY — this is the step-1 finding that changes the shape of step 4.** The only production caller of `recordAttemptRelease` is `foundation-attempt-service.ts:20`, which is precisely the file task-1879166d is editing. But that file needs **no edit**: `recordAttemptRelease(store, bound, record, request)` already receives the **store** and the **bound attempt** — everything the derivation needs. So the observation is derived INSIDE `attempt-release-disposition.ts` (already an owned path of steps 4 and 6), and `kernelRequest` stops relaying `request.safeBoundaryObserved`. **Zero edits to the collided file, no race with the peer, and no coordination note required.** That file's own comment at :70 names this task as the producer it was waiting for, so this is the seam it was written for.

**THE PREDICATE, pinned in the step-1 note before any test is written, with one refinement the plan's wording would have got wrong.** `ClaudeLaunchExit` (`claude-launcher-contract.ts:112-115`) is a THREE-arm union — `EXITED`, `SIGNALLED`, and **`UNOBSERVED`** — so `exit !== null` is NOT sufficient: `{kind:"UNOBSERVED"}` is a non-null exit whose entire meaning is that the host did not see the boundary crossed. `safeBoundaryObserved` is TRUE only when the record is decodable AND `launch.truthClass === "PROVEN"` AND `launch.exit` is `EXITED`-or-`SIGNALLED` AND `terminal !== "UNKNOWN"` AND `launch.completedAt !== null`. Record present but any clause failing → **false**, with a code naming the failing clause. Record absent or unreadable → **typed UNKNOWN**, nothing recorded. `PROCESS_OBSERVED`, `FoundationAttemptRecorded` and `intakeProcessObservation` are excluded by name.

comments.author: qa-a533e802
comments.content:
QA residual, filed durably at approval (qa-a533e802). NOT a rejection reason — the DoD's named conditions are all met and now all five drilled. Recording it because it is real, I measured it, and it would otherwise live only in an approval summary.

THE EDGE: `derivedAt`'s new third fallback can THROW instead of refusing.

  safe-boundary-observation.ts:180-184
    const wall = run.record.observedStart?.serverWallSeconds;
    const derivedAt = launch.completedAt ?? launch.startedAt
      ?? (typeof wall === "number" && Number.isFinite(wall)
        ? new Date(wall * 1_000).toISOString() : null);

`Number.isFinite` is not sufficient. The upstream admission bounds `serverWallSeconds` only as a
non-negative SAFE INTEGER — `provider-run-codec.validation.ts:60-62`, `count()` = `typeof number
&& Number.isSafeInteger && >= 0`, no upper bound. Measured in node:

  serverWallSeconds = 8.64e12       -> "+275760-09-13T00:00:00.000Z"   (last valid)
  serverWallSeconds = MAX_SAFE_INT  -> RangeError: Invalid time value  (throws)

So a durable record carrying `serverWallSeconds > 8.64e12` with BOTH `launch.completedAt` and
`launch.startedAt` null reaches `.toISOString()` and throws. A crash is not a refusal, and this
module's whole contract is that unreadable evidence becomes a typed UNKNOWN — the same principle
the `wall:<n>` defect you just fixed was violating, one layer further out.

WHY I DID NOT REJECT ON IT: no production writer emits such a value (it is ~275,000 years of wall
seconds), so no honest fixture reaches the branch — unlike the `wall:<n>` defect, which ordinary
data hit. It is hostile-input hardening beyond anything the DoD names, and rejecting a row that
just closed a real fail-silent defect, over a branch nothing can currently reach, would be
disproportionate.

IF SOMEONE HARDENS IT: the total form is a bounded conversion — reject the value unless
`wall * 1_000` is within ±8.64e15 — refusing `SAFE_BOUNDARY_RUN_UNREADABLE` /
`NO_DURABLE_INSTANT` exactly as the null path already does, so the branch stays fail-closed
rather than fail-fast. Alternatively bound `count()` upstream, which fixes the class rather than
this instance. Either way it wants a test that drives it, or it becomes the sixth arm nobody
drilled.
